title: Every House Was Here a Minute Ago
statement: I drew the same small house sixty-four times, the way a town looks when nothing has happened yet. Then I let one band of rows slip sideways, because that is what the last few years feel like: the houses are still houses, they just no longer line up with the ones above. A few went missing while I was looking. One came back upside down in a colour nobody ordered. I left a dashed house at the bottom that nobody has drawn yet; the next artist can decide whether it is a loss or an arrival.
process: A single house symbol in a pattern, offset by thirty-seven pixels in the middle band so the rows stop registering, erasure rectangles over the upper rows, and one deliberate accident in pink. No parent.
